entries.description: First-row insert race (theoretical): SELECT FOR UPDATE LIMIT 1 acquires no lock when WHERE matches 0 rows. Two concurrent sessions inserting the FIRST-EVER ledger row for the same (design, grade) can each succeed at running_balance=delta. Once per (design, grade) lifetime. **Likely subsumed by TD-011's advisory-lock fix** since pg_advisory_xact_lock acquires even when no row exists. Re-verify in S3.

7 frontend tests (TC-092/093/095/097/099/101/102) cannot exercise Radix UI Select / Popover interactions in jsdom — portals + internal state machinery don't fully materialize. Matches S1's TC-045 deferral. 6 zod-direct sibling TCs in the same files pass cleanly. Resolution options: (a) mock @radix-ui/react-select with native <select> shim in jest.setup.ts, (b) move to Playwright/Cypress E2E in S3+, (c) accept as scaffold-level coverage (backend API tests cover the same ACs).

PostgreSQL SELECT ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE does NOT re-resolve LIMIT after waiting on a row lock — the waiter re-reads the originally-identified (now-stale) row, missing the row just inserted by the holder. Surfaced by ST-007 with 2-session concurrency test. **Closed in-step** by adding pg_advisory_xact_lock(design_id, grade_id) BEFORE the FOR UPDATE in src/domain/stock.py::_apply. DS-002 spec text in decisions.json should be amended in S3 to mandate the advisory-lock-first layered pattern (see FA-S2-002/003).

entries.title: DS-002 spec text vs implementation drift
entries.description: TD-011 implementation (advisory-lock-first) is correct, but DS-002 spec text still describes only 'SELECT FOR UPDATE on latest row' without mentioning the advisory lock requirement. Risk: future contributor implements a new write path mirroring DS-002 text and re-introduces the LIMIT-1 race. Mitigation: amend DS-002 text in S3 /ases-lld.
